name: Chroma Grid
description: A grayscale gallery that gains color under a follow spot: only within the light's radius do the photos show their true hue and their edges show their own accent color.
interactionNotes: The spotlight follows the pointer with an adjustable lag and, on exit, turns off over the "fade out" of a second or so. In "card" mode, instead of a global light, hovering each card colors only that card. The light coordinates are physical and need no mirroring in RTL; the texts lay out right-to-left by themselves.

props.name: items
props.description: The cards; each has `image` (required), `title`, `subtitle`, `accent` (the edge glow hue) and an optional `url`. Without them, six sample cards appear.

props.name: columns
props.description: The grid columns; combined with `minCardWidth`, and at a low width it reduces by itself.

props.name: minCardWidth
props.description: Minimum width of each card, pixels.

props.name: softness
props.description: Softness of the light's edge; zero is a sharp disc, one is a complete blur from the center.

props.name: damping
props.description: The lag of the light's pursuit; zero sticks to the pointer.

props.name: fadeOut
props.description: The time in seconds to turn off after the pointer leaves.

props.name: grayscale
props.description: How grayscale the normal state is; 0 means always colored.

props.name: glow
props.description: The hue of the light that settles on the card under the spotlight.

props.name: borderGlow
props.description: Glow of the card edges in their own hue.

props.name: reveal
props.description: A global light under the pointer, or each card coloring independently on hover.

props.name: aspectRatio
props.description: Image ratio of the cards; such as "1 / 1" or "16 / 10".

props.name: showInfo
props.description: The title and subtitle on the cards.

props.name: theme
props.description: Palette of the frame and the tiles.

tips: Each card's `accent` hue is visible only under the light: the card's edge and the colored wash beneath the image light up in that same hue — great for the gallery's visual categorization (each topic a hue).
`reveal="card"` is better for touch rows: a global spotlight makes no sense on a touch screen and each card colors independently on hover.
Halve `grayscale` so the gallery stays "colored by cool light" — it gives an appealing middle state that is neither black and white nor fully colored.
With a long `fadeOut`, the light's shutdown becomes drawn out and cinematic; with zero it is instant — for busy galleries instant is better.
It has no dependency and no permanent rAF loop: the light's falloff is a pre-built 13-stop gradient that only moves with two coordinate variables.
